witness_description: Let G1 = G2 be the undirected simple labeled graph with the single vertex labeled 0 and no edges. Its maximal common subgraph is that same one-vertex graph, but the displayed definition produces the empty set.
refutation_explanation: For any common subgraph G, the universal quantifier permits G_* = G. By reflexivity of the subgraph relation, G_* >= G then holds, contradicting the required G_* not >= G. Thus the displayed predicate rejects every common subgraph, including the maximal graph in the concrete witness.
search_space: Exhaustive sweep of the sole ordered host pair (G1, G2) in which both hosts are the undirected simple labeled graph with vertex set {0} and no edges. Both graphs over the label universe {0}—the empty graph and the one-vertex graph—were tested as subgraph candidates, with <= implemented by vertex and edge inclusion.
